adds.title: ILGA-Europe Annual Report - Romania ranking 2022 / 2026
adds.summary: In Romania during January-December 2025 legal gender recognition had no fair, transparent self-determination-based framework free from abusive requirements with a non-binary option, with the 7 June 2025 Bucharest Pride march of approximately 31,000 people during the first full Pride Month demanding simplified legal gender recognition procedures, civil union legislation, and protection against hate speech and prejudice-based crimes; hate crime and hate speech protections lacked express coverage of sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression and sex characteristics; during the 2025 presidential campaign Prime Minister Marcel Ciolacu opposed amendments to identity documents to accommodate legal gender recognition as creating confusion and eroding traditional norms, and in October 2025 political figures claimed children could choose their gender without parental consent following the European Commission LGBTI Equality Strategy 2026-2030 recommendations; in October 2025 three training-of-trainers sessions were held for police officers, prosecutors and social workers to recognise, investigate and respond to hate crimes targeting LGBTI people; on 5 June 2025 B1 TV's News Pass framed Pride as a provocation with derogatory portrayals of LGBTI visibility, resulting in an August 2025 public warning from the National Audiovisual Council for breach of the Audiovisual Code prohibition on generalised defamatory statements against groups defined by sexual orientation; July 2025 Oradea Pride proceeded despite a third-year municipal ban attempt under heavy police supervision with nine organisers and participants fined and a subsequent application to the European Court of Human Rights, while Pride events in Cluj-Napoca, Brasov, Timisoara and Iasi took place without incidents.

adds.title: Emergency Ordinance no. 89/2001 repealing Penal Code Art. 200
adds.summary: Emergency Ordinance No. 89/2001 adopted 21 June 2001 and in force 26 June 2001 repealed Penal Code Article 200 thereby decriminalizing consensual adult same-sex sexual relations and redefined Articles 197, 198, 201 and 202 in gender-neutral terms applying equally to sexual acts with persons of different sex or same sex, with pending investigations/trials and custodial sentences under former Article 200(2)-(4) to be maintained only if the facts were also punishable under other Penal Code or special-law provisions with reclassification by the execution court.
